utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, let's start your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I hope that we will have enough time to shed more light on all the questions that you came here to testify about. Tell me, where did you exactly live in Velesici?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this day, I live in Muhameda Efendija Bandzije, and that is the former Lovcenska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at a city map. You can actually show that location, can you not?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that Gornji or Donji Velesici?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Donji Velesici.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P815. In e-court, P815. Can I now please ask for this central part, the right-hand center of this map, to be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the quality of this exhibit is as good as the other one. How about trying 13567.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I trust your knowledge, so let's have that map. Let us try to zoom in on that very same part above these red numbers. Right, that would be it. Now the left half, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We saw Velesici in the upper left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, yes, the central part now, could all of that be enlarged. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see your own coordinates on this map, Mr. Begic?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Velesici [indicating].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not that part, the central part. Could you go down a bit more. Thank you. I think we have all we need now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you please wait for the pen to be activated for you.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put a small X on the location where your house was and where it still is; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, somewhere around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What are these buildings right below the circle that you described?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnalijek factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around it and put a number there? Let's say number 2. Let your house be number 1 and Bosnalijek number 2.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that would be it [marks], approximately, because the factory goes from Bare to Velesici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark this as number 2, and your house is number 1.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Bosnalijek manufactured explosives during the war?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what is this, south of this circle that you drew, underneath the circle, the two rectangular buildings?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I could answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the Zegrep [phoen] Hotel or something like that?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, possibly. It may be the Grand Hotel, the Zegrep Hotel, as it used to be called.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot feel sure about doing this, but I think it may be somewhere around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put a number 3 there?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the ZGP used for during the war?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As far as I know, it wasn't operating on a commercial basis. I really cannot say what it was used for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it made available to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where that car repairs shop is below number 3, car repair?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that you're talking about the one within the School of Traffic and Transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you put a circle around there?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's roughly here [marks], close to the Grand Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 4 there? Could you please put number 4 there on that location where the repair shop is, the service station? Does the pen work?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pen does work. But I'm telling you, once again, I cannot say with any certainty that that is where it is on this map. But, okay, I'll put a number 4 there [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right - thank you - that a bit further down is the Fabrika Alija Hodzic, Alhos, the Alhos factory?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not in Velesici. It belongs to the neighbourhood of Kosevsko Brdo. It is a factory opposite the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to put a circle around that factory?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where to put the circle. I cannot see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that you had to pass by it, especially when you went down Kalemova, underneath the C, where the word "Centar" is?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Centrotrans, do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Centrotrans is at Stup.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But part of it is here, behind Alija Hodzic; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not Centrotrans. That is part of the city transportation company where buses park.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, since you passed that way every day, could you please put a circle around that, that is to say, around the Alhos complex and the car park or bus park? Am I right that that is next to the letter C, where it says "Centar Sarajevo"?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's approximately somewhere around here [marks]. Kosevsko Brdo, I'm telling you, that is the lower part of Kosevsko Brdo, the Alhos factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Opposite the railway station -- could you put a circle around the railway station, the whole complex, as it were? Do you see the railroad there and the big building of the railway station?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably here [indicating].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not really. Behind the Marsal Tito Barracks; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, yes, yes. Then it's this [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You put a circle around the railway station and the car park or bus park.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is 150 or 200 metres away from the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Alhos what remained outside the circle, in respect of this long building?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a circle around Crni Vrh? You see it is written there, and you see the elevation.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I have put a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that within number 4, you also put a circle around the exit out of Velesici Tunnel?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I am not very good with maps at all. It is close to that neighbourhood. However, the tunnel is between Velesici and Kosevsko Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now mark where your first unit was, the first unit that you were in? If I'm not mistaken, that is where the streets of Mose Pijade and Nemanjina merge. Those are the former names.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put a small circle there? You see Mejtas, you see the central park, you see the police building; do you see all of that?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see Kosevo, but I don't really know where to put a circle. I was roughly in those streets that you referred to just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say you can see the beginning of the cemetery there, Lav, and then two faculties, and then Nemanjina is a bit further down, and then Mose Pijade, right, Kosevsko nowadays?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is roughly somewhere around here [marks], but I cannot say that with any degree of certainty. I think it would be around there, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that is Ciglane. Can you go back to Titova Street or, rather, the main park, the big park there?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's here [indicating].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The big park, the police building, and then Nemanjina Street, leading to Bolnicka; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is Kosevo, but I cannot see Nemanjina. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the park and Titova Street, Mejtas, the police building?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that. Now I see it. Mejtas, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you take Nemanjina in order to get to Mose Pijade Street?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, somewhere around there, around Mejtas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see Trampina next to the park? Do you know where Trampina Street was?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It rings a bell, but I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: By the Kljuc factory, by the Park Restaurant?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that where the Command of the 105th Brigade is?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. I cannot answer. I do not know the answer to that question. I was no commander in order to be able to know where the command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So from your house, you went to your unit every day; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us how it was?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first six months, I slept there. I came home every five or six days or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did you go between these two locations?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the house to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Dentistry School, where your unit was.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the tunnel, through Ciglane. Then I passed by the big park, and I get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your participation in the armed forces is registered from when?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the name of your unit?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina until 1993, and then I was transferred to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This initial part, what was the name of your unit?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Afterwards, did it become part of some brigade, that battalion?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. However, I had already left the unit in March 1993. I was transferred to the police, the Novo Sarajevo Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the army or the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The army. We are talking about the period when you were in the army.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adnan Solakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Wasn't it already in 1992 that that unit became part of the 105th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us now, please, whether there were any military objectives -- actually, were there any military facilities, military objectives, military units, in Velesici?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think there was one, the former depot of the JNA. After that, the Delta Unit was there. That is at the very entrance to Velesici. If we're talking about the army, you can call that a military objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's in your street; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was in your street, in Lovcenska?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you use a blue marker in order to change colours? Could you mark the depot with a blue pen, where the Delta Unit was?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say somewhere here [marks] at the beginning. Here, right at the beginning, at the very entrance to Velesici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a number? How many numbers did we use up? That would be number 5.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it true that in this service station, police and army vehicles were repaired and maintained?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any tanks in Velesici?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know. At least I never saw one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a tank in the tunnel? Did it ever come out into the Velesici side, fired, and then went back into the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Somewhere on the picture, right above Grbavica or Debelo Brdo, can you put today's date and your initials?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said to put it near Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no. In the bottom of the picture, where it wouldn't be in the way, near Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What am I to put?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date and your initials or signature.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now look at Crni Vrh. Do you know there was a howitzer there?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D930. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can Mr. Karadzic put time-frames on his questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Begic, that this position of confrontation lines and forces in Sarajevo remained more or less the same from the beginning to the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a military expert. I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you're a soldier and a policeman. Do you know of any significant changes, apart from renaming brigades, significant changes of positions in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Velesici and the neighbouring area and all these locations, were they all the time in the hands of the BH Army or were there times when the Serbs held them?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were always in the hands of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you referring to this map, marked map? That has been already admitted. It was announced as D930. But what is your question, after having all the exercise of marking various places?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we can remove this map. But I wanted -- Ms. Sutherland wanted a time-frame, and I wanted to establish that the situation in Sarajevo did not change during the war at all, so it doesn't matter which period in the war it was. Can we now see D585.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please remember that you have only an hour for your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. But by extending the testimony to Velesici, the Defence has come to face a new task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to read this paragraph that begins with the words: "In the Velesici tunnel ..."? Mr. Begic, may I ask you to read this aloud? Do you see, for instance, that in Velesici, there was a tank, whereas in front of the building of the BH TO at Ciglane there is an APC and a tank, in the Gornji Velesici area, the forces of the BH TO are positioned, and the police station is in the Local Commune building in Velesici. And below the TV relay --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not following. This is going too fast. Mr. Karadzic needs to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, your words were not interpreted. You were too fast, and the interpreters couldn't follow. We can read it. What is your question? That has been admitted. Put your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is testing the credibility of this witness. He was a soldier and a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know all these streets --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know all these streets? Your street is mentioned here and these localities, the bus terminal, Kosevo Hill, Local Commune, Velesici, the police station. Do you know them all?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since I was born in Sarajevo, of course I know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that you did not see tanks, guns, artillery, that you did not know all the places where the army was deployed in Velesici?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. We're talking about the tunnel which I used to pass through. You asked me a moment ago how I went to work. There were two tunnels, one by the other. One was completely unusable. It hasn't been open to this day. How would I know where the tanks were positioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If there was shooting on Velesici, if a shell exploded, would you hold that Velesici was being targeted as a civilian neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Why would one shoot at private houses if one didn't want to hit civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Begic. Do you deny that throughout -- below Velesici and below Hum, there was a tank and mortars, they were active, that the military had their installations there, repairing and maintaining their vehicles? Do you deny that?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just don't have that knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see P1477, to see what Mladic meant when he spoke about Velesici. This is 25th May 1992. Can we see page 389, and in English it would be 380.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We can see it here. Do you see this date, "Monday, 25th May 1992," "Interview with Wilson," et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the date "18 May 1992" on the right-hand page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry. Is it possible we could have the English translation on -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, do you understand what this is about? This is General Mladic's diary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can make out some of it, because it's written in Cyrillic. I can understand it, partially, and I've learnt Cyrillic. But I haven't used it in a long time, so it's kind of difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about this first page. Does it relate to Monday, 25th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that date towards the bottom, but I cannot read the upper part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland. The English page does not --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- show the proper page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 380 in English, 380. In Serbian, can we now see 389?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can have the appropriate English page. But also the witness has just said that he doesn't fully understand Cyrillic, and so he needs to have the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I agree. So, first of all, can we have the proper English page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 380, please. I think Mr. Begic is literate, he's learned Cyrillic. We need the Serbian page 389, and, if necessary, I will read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me confirm. Can you read Cyrillic, Mr. Begic? You said your knowledge is limited or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's been 20 years that I haven't read or written in Cyrillic script. So I can read part of it, but not all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us up-load the B/C/S version in Latin. We have to find 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't expect this. That means we need more time. I can read this, and Mr. Begic can just double-check that I'm reading correctly. I think we have the right page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the initial page. It says "Monday, 25th May 1992."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the English page 394 and the Serbian page 403. 403 is the handwritten page, the manuscript. This is the English. Right, we have the Serbian now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read to us this little passage at the bottom that says: "Hardware and population ..."? Can you read it aloud, please?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Hardware and population, opening fire at enemy military targets and buildings from which the attack on the MT Barracks and positions of the SRK members was being commanded."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see that intercept, 65 ter 35001. It must have been admitted and must have a P number, but it's -- 35001 is the 65 ter. This has been exhibited, hasn't it? 65 ter 35001.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General Mladic is talking to one of his subordinates, and he says: "Fire" at such and such locality. Do you understand that to mean that they don't know what they are shooting at or they are shooting randomly?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that they're targeting "Velosici." It probably means Velesici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What there?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Fire at Velesici. There is no Serbian population there."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this. When he says: "Do you have a target you've honed in on there"?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written: "Do you have it or don't you?"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we raise the page in English to read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Where can you fire?" "I cannot fire here close to the barracks." And the other says: "No, no, not close to the barracks. Can you fire at Velesici?" And the other one says: "I can." And the first person says: "Do you have a ranged-in target there?" Person number 2 says: "Yes, I do."

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean that he's to shoot at Velesici, as such, or a target in Velesici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need a second -- the next page in English. It started from the bottom of this page. Yes, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, is it clear to you that it's not anything that's being fired at in Velesici, but a target that is marked on the map; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not right, because you hit I don't know how many houses, 300, 400, 500 houses, and you killed I don't even know how many of my neighbours. So you should have just targeted this one military objective, without destroying 500 houses and I don't know how many people in my neighbourhood and in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, I'm just asking you about what Mladic says here, not about what happened. Is it clear here that Mladic is referring to a specific target in Velesici, not Velesici as a whole?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see what target it is. "Do you have a ranged-in target?" Maybe I was the target, maybe my neighbour was a target. Where does it say what was the target or who was the target?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look at this in the light of the diary that we looked at a moment ago, is it not clear that these are military objectives?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I understand. D027, could we have that now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think this exhibit has been tendered previously.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be admitted, if possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we mark it for identification, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 35001 shall be assigned Exhibit D931, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have an intercept now, one that Mladic recognises as his own, D207, in e-court. D207.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a conversation between Mladic and Potpara and Mladic and Baros, on the 29th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Towards the bottom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, did you say Mladic recognised this intercept as his own? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will see, Excellency, from the document itself, that Mladic is commenting upon something else that is being ascribed to him. He is talking to two of his subordinates, and he is commenting upon something else that is being ascribed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, do you see the third line from the bottom? Mladic says: "They want to provoke us to hit town by attacking our barracks." Potpara says: "Yes, right." And Mladic says: "Tell people that so that they would know." Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written here, but only God knows what the truth may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please ensure that we are following. We need the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In English, you can already see it: "Be careful ..." and so on. Can we now have page 4. This has already been admitted. The Chamber has seen it, the participants have seen it. I just wanted to show it to you. Page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that up here Mladic is saying that they violated part of the agreement? In English, it's page 8, actually. Have a look at it. We're not going to read it. They violated it. Then 54 vehicles have been sheltered: "Don't receive any emissaries. No one ..." And so on and so forth. And: "Please exercise restraint." Do you see that Mladic is asking them to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, really do look at the question of time. Could that please be reconsidered, because the Prosecution expanded the importance of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this lower part, what Ratko Mladic says here: "I feel the same way." Can you read that out?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Me too, I have the same opinion. If they want peace, they --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 8 in English so that the participants can follow what it is that you're reading: [In English] "I share the same opinion." [Interpretation] Please go on.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I share the same opinion. We think in the same way. If they want peace, they will have it. I ordered, as soon as I came back last night. It was an all-out attack against the units and you. There was shooting, and somehow I managed to calm down the people there, to put everything under control, to stop the fire. As for what they are producing now, they probably have pantomime performers, some good imitators who are able to imitate our voices properly, I mean your voice, my voice, and anyone's voice."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the two passages further down?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask you something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's been 15 minutes now that I have been testifying. I have not been asked a single question by Karadzic in relation to the reasons why I came here to testify; Markale, my father, and so on. I have not come here to read this. I have no idea who wrote this and what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, I understand how you feel, but the accused is entitled to put any questions which was raised in your examination-in-chief. You dealt with the shelling of Velesici, and you talked about the Mladic diary, so he's entitled to cross-examine you as robust as he can. So I appreciate your understanding, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Whilst I agree with the President, of course, as to the accurate observations that are made, it seems to me, Dr. Karadzic, that it would be far better for everybody concerned in the case if you were to concentrate on the issues that the witness really came here to discuss. The issues raised in the Mladic diaries can be adequately dealt with, and perhaps more profitably dealt with, in another way with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. And just to correct something you said, that he talked about the Mladic diary in his statement. He talked about the Mladic intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I fully agree, but I've seen some judgements where it says, Yes, it has been established, but some other witness said this and that and the other thing. That's why I cannot leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Move on, please, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, could you please tell me which part of his leg your father exactly lost in the railway accident.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His entire foot. That is to say, he did not have a foot, and the prosthesis was up to his knee. All disabled people who did not have a foot had to have that kind of prosthetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was the cut, exactly?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd need to show that, so I'd have to get up and to show it to you, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to pause for the interpretation. Can you tell me how much from the ankle?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two centimetres above the ankle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the entire lower leg was still there?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How tall are you, Mr. Begic?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One metre seventy-nine centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How tall was your late father?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My late father was about 1.80.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which hospital did you go to when you went to visit your father?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the French hospital, where they had transferred him from the Kosevo Hospital, but I didn't manage to see him there. At 4.15, my father passed away, so I didn't manage to see him there. I only saw him in the morgue of the Kosevo Hospital on that same day, during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the prosthesis -- you took it over two days after the explosion. Is that one day after the funeral? That's what you were saying during your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been 16 years now. I cannot say exactly whether it was a day or two or three, but it was immediately after the funeral. After the funeral, I took over the prosthesis in the Sarajevo market or shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to ask you and to remind myself to pause between our exchanges so that the interpreters manage to interpret all of this properly. So when I am quiet, would you please understand that to be that kind of pause.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we have that prosthesis now?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you mean, "now"; this very instant here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in Sarajevo. I own it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When were you first asked about it?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question? When was I asked by who about the prosthesis?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When were you first asked about it in any investigation?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find the question to be a bit unclear. But immediately after the explosion of the shell, in our federal MUP I said that it was my father's prosthesis and that I have it at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And as for this Tribunal, you never spoke about it until my opening statement; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I waited for many, many years for you to be arrested and to come to The Hague, and it was only then that I could come to The Hague and say that I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And none of them asked you before you volunteered; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is your knowledge about the number of casualties at Markale I in February?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every person who got killed at Sarajevo market has his or her name written on the plaque, memorial plaque in Markale. I'm there every year, so all the names and surnames of the persons who got killed there are carved there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, to the best your knowledge, how many casualties there were. You were a policeman by then, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many persons were killed?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 67 or 68 persons. I think it is 67.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many were wounded? Almost 200; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was about 200 people who were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Didn't you find it unusual that there were so many people in a market-place where there were no goods?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't find that to be unusual, because I spent the entire war in the town of Sarajevo. Markets were always full, except when there was frequent shelling and when the police would ask people to leave. But in markets, there were lots and lots of people all the time, because life in Sarajevo, as a whole, took place in these market-places. It's not true that there were no goods there. You could buy, I don't know, tins and cigarettes and whatever else at markets, and there was practically bartering going on in these market-places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to have a look, and you're going to see that the market-place was empty, there were no goods whatsoever there from the very outset. But tell us, please, how long was your father's prosthesis?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that with any certainty. I can only measure it and then tell you how long it is, because I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did the inside of the prosthesis look like?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you mean? Every disabled person who had a prosthetic leg had to have these special socks, if I can call them that, 50 or 60 centimetres long, so that the prosthetic leg could be worn that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please -- you saw that film yesterday, the moment when the prosthetic leg was being thrown and then brought back. What was the point of it being thrown, and what was the point of having it returned to the market?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. But you should have heard the words of the man who is throwing the prosthesis and why he is doing that and what he is saying. Just listen to the words. The man is in shock, and just listen carefully to what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let us play a clip from that film. Let's see the photograph, 1D2897, 2897.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, do you see that this prosthetic leg is approximately the same height as the height between the knee of this man and the ground?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the next one, 2898. Can this photograph be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D932. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2897. Sorry, 98.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Begic, that this man on the right-hand side comes up to the mid-ear of this person carrying the prosthetic leg?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't see the prosthesis at all in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The middleman is carrying it. You can see the shoe on it.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But these are very tall people, Mr. Begic, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the man carrying the prosthesis is above 180 centimetres tall? He's taller than you are; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the picture, he seems to be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this photograph be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D933.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next one, 65 ter 23014.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this man carrying the prosthesis?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 23014.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, can we see your late father?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is he wearing the light-colour suit or the dark colour?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dark jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are they on a bridge in a big European city?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I can't tell you with any certainty which city it was. It's a neighbouring country of the former Yugoslavia, Bulgaria or Hungary. I don't know where he went on a trip with his neighbour, Hilmo. But you can see that my father is disabled and that he's wearing his prosthetic leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the railing on this bridge is between 100 and 110 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot answer this kind of question that you're putting, that you keep putting, and I cannot determine how high the railing is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? Oh, it's already exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- would you say that your father was of average height or above average?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's average, 180, 181 centimetres. I would say it's average.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, that is Exhibit P02052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D02899, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It seems to me, Mr. Begic, that he, your late father, was much shorter than you are saying. Look at these ratios in Auto-CAD.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who made this for you. I know that my father was approximately as tall as I am. Yes, when people age, they get a little shorter than they were when they were young, but he was not shorter than 180.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that the size of the lower leg would be 44 to 48 centimetres if he was as tall as you say? And I'm not sure you are correct about 180 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he was around 180 centimetres' tall. It could have been one centimetre less or more, but I know how tall my father was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you agree this is the height of the railing, the length of the lower leg and the height of Camil Begic in the third column.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How on earth can the witness agree the height of this railing is something? Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, that was my point, Your Honour. The witness has just said that he can't give any indication as to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Not only that, Dr. Karadzic, it strikes me that all this debate is predicated upon the basis that we know exactly how far the deceased's leg went into the prosthesis and how much above the knee the prosthesis may have extended in order to support the joint. We have no evidence at all of that, and inevitably that's going to make a variable and substantial difference. So I'm not sure of the value of this exercise at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm coming back to that. The railing's a standard height in Europe, 100, 110 centimetres, but we'll leave that aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, do you know that placing the entire lower leg into this prosthesis would be uncomfortable and inconvenient, and it would be a single tall boot, too much just to replace a foot?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you -- can this question be repeated to me, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you, as a doctor, that this high boot is not the prosthesis that would be given to someone who lost just one foot, and placing his whole leg into this prosthesis would be detrimental, not only uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. It was made in the Orthopaedics Clinic. Dr. Kulenovic made it as soon as he got the right material. Most disabled people lost a lot of weight during the war, and my father, too, so he didn't really fit. He was too thin for the prosthesis he got at first, so he was given a new one later on, three months later. And I went to the Neretva, the company which made prostheses, and showed it to Dr. Kulenovic to see if something could be done. And the new one, the new prosthesis, was a lot lighter, and people walked in these prosthetic legs much more easily. That's the one my father had during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now see the inside of that prosthetic leg, and we'll look at the standard measurements. Can we now see a photograph -- or, rather, a clip. We'll bring a new expert here. This is part of a video-clip, P1984.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, Mr. Begic -- do you see that this prosthesis is shallow?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you are seeing, but I know this is my father's prosthetic leg.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The shell that fell around 1200 hours killed a lot of people, and many are seriously wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, how can you explain that the entire lower leg of your father fit into this, when you see that the bottom of this prosthesis is 10 centimetres from the edge?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, allow me to get up and show you up to which height, exactly, my father was missing his leg. And I just explained to Karadzic that there were two socks that were pulled over the stump so you can put your leg into the prosthesis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, just a second. So that the camera can follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you go back a bit. Can you just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would the Audio-Video Unit show him? Yes, please go on. You can turn on -- you can speak, probably. I think the interpreters could follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This -- my father was missing this whole bit above this bone. He was missing this part [indicates]. The leg was up to here [indicates]. It even got narrower. That is the part he was missing. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Begic. I have a lot of understanding and respect for you and your loss, but this is not the prosthesis, Mr. Begic. You know that there are low boots and high boots, and it would be very bad to give such a high boot to a man who has his entire lower leg.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the prosthesis. What else can we establish? I believe there are 10, perhaps 12, holes of shrapnel in this prosthesis. In one of these holes, some shrapnel should still be present. I'm not a military expert, but if you had military experts, why don't you give it -- give this prosthesis to the military experts, and let them establish whether the shrapnel belongs to that shell. And then you will see it's my father's.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic has to repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could there have been other prosthetic legs on the market on that day?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I know? I cannot answer that question. Maybe there were other disabled people there. Maybe other people got killed there wearing their prosthetic legs and the prosthetic legs did not fall off. I can't know that. But I know this is my father's prosthetic leg.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now display the clip from 1 hour 17 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting: Did you notice some uniformed and some armed people?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Those were the soldiers who came to help remove the dead bodies and help the wounded. Those are people who ran to other people's aid. You saw the vehicles that were stopping. Most of these young men were in uniform, those who were carrying the bodies and the wounded into cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How come they were so near and were there to run there so quickly?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I wasn't there. But everyone who was nearby ran to the place after the massacre to help the wounded be transported to hospitals, to help carry the dead away. That was a common-place thing for us at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see what this participant in the evacuation says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You heard this participant say, They will say that we did it?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to hear it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Never mind. Did you hear that he counted 25 dead?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't hear. Can you replay it, and then I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you hear he says he counted 25 dead?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that he saw 25 dead. He didn't say how many were carried away before he arrived. He just talked about what he had seen. He couldn't have known how many people had been already carried to the morgue before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you'll have five minutes to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the traces of dragging here?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Traces of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that somebody was dragged here?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You obviously don't know what "massacre" means. How else would you deal with it in a place like this? You have to take a butchered body and drag it onto a blanket. People were torn to pieces, and it was everywhere between these stalls. People were torn to pieces.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play just a little more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why does this person take out the plastic sheet from underneath this man? Do you see that this man was dragged here on a plastic sheet, and then the plastic sheet was pulled out?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that this man sees the victim is already dead, is taking the plastic sheet to use it to help someone else who is still alive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I see. Now we'll see another part that relates to the prosthesis. 1D2895.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain that this prosthetic leg is standing up here?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given it a lot of thought. I've been watching this footage for 16 years and thinking, and I'm kind of making my own movie in my mind because it bothers me. The market has been cleared, the shelling is over. I think, because a war is going on, nobody has any money. People are prepared to do anything. I think that in exchange for two or three tin cans of food, somebody offered a journalist to -- a photograph of this prosthetic leg. You can see that the market has been cleaned, there is nothing on it. This is my father's prosthetic leg. I am absolutely sure that one of the photo reporters asked somebody to place it there to make a photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how long did it take to clean up the market?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really don't know. I wasn't present there to be able to answer the question how long it took to clean up. I wasn't there, and I can't answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We'll play a video-clip and watch it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, Mr. Begic, that there is no one there, there's nothing? Everything is implausibly empty.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am saying, with full responsibility, that this is an image after the massacre. Everything has been cleared. I'm saying this under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's play that part again with the blood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Is that strictly necessary, Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, all of this was staged by the police where Mr. Begic worked. I'm not saying it was his unit, but we know full well who worked in that unit and who staged all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: That is -- it's not your giving evidence, because it's not evidence, it's simply a comment. If you've got another pertinent question to ask of this witness, then please do so, but it seems to me that re-running videos that we've all seen many times is really not going to assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I just ask you once again, Mr. Begic, please focus on this passageway where the man is walking with the prosthesis. Are there any traces of dragging there, of the evacuation of the dead and wounded? Just look at this passageway where he is entering. What does it look like?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks cleared. Just listen to what these people are saying. You will hear, from their conversation, that everything has been cleaned, that there are no blood-stains. It has been cleaned. Listen to what they are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that on the film this prosthesis is in different places? It's in the passageway, it's underneath the stall in one position, and then in a different position. Then it is being thrown, and then it is being returned; right?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I watched all of this footage over 50 times, unfortunately, over these 16 years. During the massacre, you see the prosthesis in one particular place, and I think that's exactly where my father got killed. Later on, you see it about half a metre away, underneath a stall. If so many people get killed and wounded, isn't it logical that people were passing there and that somebody, Karadzic, pushed this under the stall?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In which police department did you work from 1993 until the end of the war? What was your unit, what were your tasks?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always worked at the Police Administration of Novo Sarajevo. Wartime tasks of a policeman were that if I was not at the front-line, I worked on regular police work, keeping the law and order, if there were street fights, if there was this and that, whatever police do anywhere in the world. So if I was not on the front-line, I did regular police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did you go to the front-line?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the front-line only in Sarajevo; that is to say, I defended my own city. I never went outside Sarajevo. I was always on the lines around Sarajevo, and I defended my city honourably and honestly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All of that is well and fine, but just tell us in the zone of responsibility of which brigade. You, as the police, were attached to some mountain brigade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Police Administration of Novo Sarajevo, well, sent me to Nedzarici, to the line behind the student dormitories. That's where I would spend, say, 10 days, and then I would be resting for a month, and then for two or three days I went to the hill of Zuc because that is my municipality, and the Police Administration where I worked went several times to help out. I don't know which brigade this was, but it was the hill of Zuc, and you know full well where Zuc is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just one area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if I could have Exhibit D930. That was the map that the witness annotated this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably we would need to switch to e-court from Sanction. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, this morning you marked, in blue pen, the location of the former depot of the JNA, when Mr. Karadzic asked you, at pages 8 to 9, of military facilities in Velesici, and you said: "Yes, that's the former depot of the JNA. After that, the Delta Unit were there." Were they there at the point where -- when you heard the intercept, the Mladic intercept, at the end of May 1992? Was this unit there at that time?

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot say with certainty that I put a circle in the right location, because I'm no expert in topography and I'm not very good at maps. So I approximately put that circle there. I know very well where the place is, but I don't know whether I marked it properly on the map. I cannot give you an answer as to whether the unit was deployed there at the beginning of the war. At any rate, it's a military facility, but I really do not know who was based there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And just one other question in relation to the prosthesis. You have said earlier in your testimony that you are prepared to have the prosthetic available for inspection. Do you still stand by that? I'm sorry, you need to answer the question so it's on the record.

utterances.speaker: ALMIR BEGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Whenever you wish, the prosthesis will be made available to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Begic, that concludes your evidence. I really appreciate your kindness to come over to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. Please have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour, after which we'll hear the evidence of Mr. Overgard through videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Overgard. Do you follow the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes I can hear you and can see you. That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Overgard.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Please state your full name and your rank.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Thorbjorn Overgard, and I'm a major in the Norwegian Air Force.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Major, you provided a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, and you also testified twice before this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You, in particular, testified in the trial against Dragomir Milosevic on the 18th and the 19th January 2007; do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review this testimony in preparation of today's testimony?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, I read through it on the screen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you affirm that the testimony accurately reflects the evidence you provided to the Tribunal in the Milosevic trial?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Major, would you provide that same evidence to the Court if questioned on the same matters here today?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this testimony as 65 ter 10321 for admission under Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be admitted as Exhibit P2058. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, I would now read a brief summary of Mr. Overgard's evidence as admitted. Major Overgard was posted to Sarajevo as a United Nations Military Observer from late October 1994. After an initial posting in an area held by the Bosnian Serb forces, he was deployed in Hrasnica within the territory held by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he remained until the 1st of May, 1995. During his time in Hrasnica, Major Overgard investigated many shelling and sniping incidents. In this -- it says here "Disconnected."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay, I think we are back on line. In this time -- no, it's not. Yes. Major, we were interrupted. I continue now with the reading of the summary. In this time-period, there were casualties almost every day. The greatest number of casualties occurred during November and December 1994 as well as April 1995. Of all the shelling and sniping investigations undertaken by Major Overgard and those working with him, VRS-held territory was identified as the source of fire. Most of the shelling incidents investigated by Major Overgard involved civilian victims. All of the sniping incidents investigated by him involved civilian victims. The VRS had firing positions in the area of Ilidza and Blazuj and in the area of Lukavica. It was mainly from these directions that Hrasnica was shelled. The center of Hrasnica was a residential civilian area with no military installations. Major Overgard investigated the shelling of 7 April 1995, charged as Scheduled Shelling Incident G10. On that day, a modified air-bomb hit a residential area in the center of Hrasnica and killed a woman and wounded others. Major Overgard heard the air-bomb coming in and the explosion, and when he visited the site, he saw one house completely destroyed and eight others extensively damaged. The investigation in this incident determined that the air-bomb was fired from Serb-held territory in Ilidza. Serb forces regularly shelled and sniped at civilians using the road to Mount Igman or the bridge at Butmir. Major Overgard estimated that during his time in Hrasnica, he investigated the death of 30 to 40 civilians as a result of sniping and shelling, including the killing of two small children on the 17th of November, 1994, and the killing of a girl walking on the Igman road. Your Honours, this concludes the summary of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Overgard, I have now a few questions to put to you in addition to that? And just to start with, I mentioned, as my last sentence, the killing of a girl walking on the Igman road that you described in your evidence. Can you place this event in time? Do you know when it happened, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't remember the date exactly anymore. I haven't been able to find any -- no notes on that. But that has to be in late March, beginning of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Major, in your evidence, you mostly described the air-bomb incident of the 7th of April, 1995. And when you gave this previous testimony, you referred to statements from witnesses that you got, and also you referred to a report that you and your team drafted. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Okay. No, it's okay, I remember, and I have reviewed the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would now like to address Exhibit 65 ter 11336. That's in e-court. And as everybody can have a look at it, it is a special report from SI-1 entitled, in the subject line, "Large explosion in Hrasnica on the 7th of April, 1995."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Major Overgard, did you have an opportunity to review this report in preparation of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know this report?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us who prepared it?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was prepared by Flight Lieutenant Calum Gunn and two more colleagues from the team. He is the main drafter of this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And it says here -- there is a reference on top of it, and it says "SI-1." What does it stand for?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It stands for the name of the team, Sierra India 1, so the Sierra Igman Team 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when we go to the second page of this document, we find signatures. And is one of them your signature?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's the second one; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It is the second one, yes, Military Observer 839.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And if we go back to the first page, if you would like to do this, under paragraph 2 we find a reference to an aircraft bomb and four rockets. These findings, on what are they based?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They are based on the fragments that we found after we were allowed in to investigate the incident, and also the parts that we were shown from the BiH authorities the day after the happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in that same paragraph is also a reference that the weapon was supposedly fired from a truck in the area of Ilidza, and you also give the grid references. This information is based on what?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It's based on the damages to the houses as long -- it's caused when -- on its way to where it exploded. There were severe damages to windows all along that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if we turn again to page 2 and the fourth paragraph, there is a reference with more details of the launch of the air-bomb. And it says here "from a truck," and that then the vehicle returned to the carpet factory in Ilidza, a storage site for vehicles of the Bosnian Serb Army. Major, from which source did you get this particular detail?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: This is from -- from the local witnesses on Mount Igman that we spoke to afterwards. As I remember it, it was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And also in that same paragraph, as the last sentence, there is a reference to the UNMOs hearing the weapon coming in, and that it landed 200 metres from the location where they were staying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, that is correct. I was in the living-room of the accommodation, and we heard. It was just like a big aircraft coming in. And so we were on our way to the floor when it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And attached to the report are a number of diagrams as to the damage found and the weapon, and what the shell rest [sic] -- the air-bomb rest [sic] that were found. Who made these drawings?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was done by Calum Gunn.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I request the admission of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted as Exhibit P2059.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to address an exhibit, 65 ter 10693, which is already admitted as P1210. And it is an order by the Romanija -- Sarajevo Romanija Corps Command to the Ilidza Brigade of the 6th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Major, did you have an opportunity to review this document in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it yesterday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the first paragraph of the order, there is a reference to Muslim forces attacking the positions of the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade, in particular, the sector of the Famos factory, "for the past three days." Major, were you aware of these military activities?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
